ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: Days on the colony calendar come round once a year. Keep one three years running and it becomes a tradition people look forward to; a keeper of days on the council makes each one more of an occasion.
A day of remembrance, sad and good at once. Keep it each year, and keep the graves tidy and near enough to walk to.
Each year a colonist stays is marked, and their friends are glad of it too. It comes round on its own.
Friends who look after someone getting over an illness are remembered for it. Rest in bed gets them well a third sooner; the advisor warns when a convalescent is back at work.
A story in several parts that ended well. The World page shows the stories still unfolding, and the council's answer at each stage decides how the next one goes.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: A story that went badly. It fades on its own within ten days, and good moments in between make up for it. The World page shows the stories still unfolding, and the council's answer at each stage decides how the next one goes.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: An heirloom is a comfort as long as it's carried, more so to the heir: keep it out of the stockpile and on them. Watching a child grow up is its own reward.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: A feeling the colony started the game with, and slow to fade. Between feuding families, shared work, shared meals and a common enemy build better opinions in the meantime.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: Something the colony started the game with, and it lasts for months. The bonds it began can grow into lasting friendships; the Bonds page shows them.

A seasonal custom kept, or a day marked properly. Give the same answer two years running and it becomes a tradition that comes round every year; a keeper of days on the council makes each kept day more of an occasion.
The colony is known for the work this colonist loves, and it holds while the work goes on. The Our ways page shows how close the colony is to each name.
A vendetta ended without more blood: laid down, or the one who was taken came home. The Bonds page keeps how it ended.
